headline: The last full loading week before taper, and the cleanest one yet — lowest RPE of the whole build (2.0), tightest-judged quality sessions to date, achilles 0 all week, recovery flat to improved. Hold the plan.
review_md:
# Weekly review — Sunday 6 September 2026

**Week of 31 August–6 September. Week 7 of the Cheltenham build — the last
full loading week before taper. 14 days to race day.**

## How the week actually went

| | This week | Last week | Week before |
|---|---|---|---|
| Volume | 69.2 km | 75.2 km | 72.8 km |
| Runs | 8 | 7 | 6 |
| Elevation | 443 m | 692 m | 427 m |
| Quality time | 146 min | 148 min | 142 min |
| Easy share | 58% | 58% | 59% |
| Efficiency | 1.473 | 1.445 | 1.478 |
| Avg RPE | **2.0** | 3.4 | 2.7 |
| Avg HRV | 38.7 | 39.0 | — |
| Avg RHR | 47.6 | 47.0 | — |
| Avg sleep score | 88.4 | 85.8 | — |

Plan called for roughly 66 km (rest, easy 7, intervals 12, easy 5, easy
5/rest, tempo 17, long 20). You ran 69.2, +3.2 over — almost entirely
Monday's easy run running nearly double its target after getting lost with
Alice, offset by Friday becoming a full rest day rather than the
discretionary 5 km shakeout. `on_target_pct` reads 100 for the week —
session-shape variance, not drift.

Session-by-session, from `session_detail.json`:

- **Mon 31 Aug (easy, planned 7 km @ 5:00–5:20/km):** actual 13.1 km at
  5:34/km, avg HR 127 — got lost with Alice, "lovely recovery run." Nearly
  double the planned distance but genuinely easy throughout (slower than
  the band, not faster), so this is exactly the low-risk kind of overshoot
  the brief distinguishes from the old too-quick mileage: added easy
  volume run easy costs nothing. Achilles 0.
- **Wed 2 Sep (intervals, planned 12 km @ 3:44/km reps):** 3.58 km
  warm-up, 5x1km mean **3:38/km** (217.6 sec/km), spread 2.9 sec/km — very
  tight — drift -0.6, essentially flat. Full session 12.35 km vs 12 km
  target, matching closely. This is the session already covered in this
  week's mid-week exchange (3 Sep) — the fourth interval session in a row
  landing quicker than target while you were trying to hold back (12 Aug
  3:39, 19 Aug 3:41, 26 Aug 3:41, 2 Sep 3:38). Nothing new to re-argue: the
  answer stands — hold the paces on the table, the fitness signal already
  moved the table via VO2max 59→60, and the next update comes from
  Cheltenham's result, not a mid-session call.
- **Thu 3 Sep (easy, planned 5 km):** 5.04 km at 5:12/km, HR 130 —
  "lowest I've seen average HR at that pace." Genuinely easy, on target.
- **Fri 4 Sep:** plan allowed a 5 km shakeout or rest, conditional on
  Sunday's run going past 21 km. You took rest, and Sunday came in at
  20.3 km — under the cap that was meant to trigger it. Not a problem
  either way given how easy the rest of the week ran, but worth asking:
  was that a felt-recovery call, or pre-agreed with the group in advance
  of knowing the distance? Either is fine, just closing the loop on it.
- **Sat 5 Sep (tempo, planned 17 km, 2x20min at HM pace 3:54/km):** 3.02
  km warm-up, then two 20-minute blocks at mean **3:52/km** (232.1
  sec/km) — 2 sec/km quicker than target, and the most even goal-pace
  execution of the block: spread **0.3 sec/km**, drift -0.3, essentially
  dead flat. Total 18.4 km vs 17 km. RPE **5** — the lowest tempo RPE of
  the whole build (22 Aug and 29 Aug were both 6). Your note: "Cruised
  it, kept edging faster but think kept it more or less on target... The
  fast rs are great... thought a stitch was coming... but all was fine."
  That's the 3 Sep instruction playing out exactly as intended — 2
  sec/km is noise, not a push, and an RPE 5 on an even, on-pace goal-pace
  session is what "pace with something in reserve" is supposed to feel
  like. Worth naming as good evidence the message landed rather than
  letting it pass unremarked.
  On fuelling: gel taken before the run and again during the recovery —
  the third quality session this block with a gel tested under load (26
  Aug, 29 Aug, now this), still SiS, no GI issue beyond a stitch that
  passed. Genuine continued progress on the race-fuelling gap. But it
  also means the Puresport question from Wednesday's reply is now down to
  one realistic test window rather than two: Saturday's tempo has passed
  without a Puresport trial, so if you still want to test it before
  Cheltenham, it's Wed 9 Sep's intervals or the taper sharpener on 12
  Sep (15 min at HM pace) — either works, but it needs deciding soon.
- **Sun 6 Sep (long, planned 20 km @ 5:00–5:10/km with Meg and Alice,
  capped 20–21 km):** 20.31 km at 5:38/km, avg HR 130 — slower than the
  band, which is fine per the plan's own allowance. Decoupling **-0.46%**,
  clean, no unreliable flags, at **111.0 analysed minutes** — one of the
  longest clean continuous stretches in the whole decoupling series.
  First half 5:18/km at 131.1 HR, second half 5:19/km at 130.3 HR —
  essentially flat. RPE **1**, the lowest of any long run logged this
  year. Achilles 0. This is exactly what last week's proposal asked for —
  "the last long run of consequence before the taper... should leave you
  fresher, not emptier" — capped correctly at 20.3 km rather than
  drifting past 21 with the group. Clean on every count.

## How he's coping — data and his own words

Recovery held essentially flat through a week that was, by every
subjective measure, the easiest of the entire build: avg HRV 39.0→**38.7**
(noise), avg RHR 47.0→**47.6** (negligible), sleep score 85.8→**88.4**
(up), sleep hours 7.8→**8.1** (up). Avg RPE fell to **2.0** — lower than
any week in the dataset — while easy-day HR dropped sharply, 141.4→**129.0
bpm** (-12.4), even as easy pace slowed (4.91→5.27 min/km). Slower pace
with much lower HR is the clearest signature yet that this week was dosed,
and run, as genuinely easy at exactly the point in the block where that
matters most.

One thing worth naming rather than ignoring: this morning's overnight HRV
read 31, 8.7 points below the 7-day baseline (39.7) — the single largest
daily deviation logged this week, with nothing in `recovery_confounders`
and readiness flagged "caution." It didn't show up in execution — the long
run still came in at RPE 1 with flat, clean decoupling — so there's
nothing to act on today. But per the brief, an unexplained dip is noise
until it either resolves or repeats. Worth a plain question rather than an
assumption: anything unusual last night? If it's gone by Tuesday, this is
nothing; if it's still there into Wednesday's intervals, that's the first
real data point toward the "lengthening recovery" trend flagged last week
becoming a genuine pattern rather than a rounding blip.

On that trend specifically: `recovery_log.json` still reads "lengthening"
from last week's read (2.3→3.0 days), and this week's two quality sessions
(2 Sep intervals, 5 Sep tempo) are both still `pending` — not enough days
have passed to confirm recovery either way. Nothing changes about that
read this week; it just carries forward as a watch item into the final
loading days.

## Achilles

0 every day this week, no mention in any note, on the lightest-feeling
week of the block by RPE. Worth confirming as usual, especially heading
into the last hard session before taper: any first-steps stiffness, or an
ache standing up from the desk, since the last two big weeks? If genuinely
nothing, that's a strong signal to carry into the final stretch.

## Heat and asthma

Today's long run carried "high" heat risk (27.4°C forecast) with no
breathing complaint, consistent with the rest of the block. The forecast
cools sharply for the week ahead — moderate to low through 9–12
September — so heat is less of a live factor for the last quality session
and the taper. The Symbicort/asthma-nurse timing conversation is now 14
days out and narrowing further given the cumulative-weeks mechanism for
inhaled preventers — still not something to settle here, just flagging the
clock is getting shorter.

## Efficiency trend

1.219 (June base) → 1.478 (17–23 Aug) → 1.445 (24–30 Aug) → **1.473** this
week. Broadly flat across the last three weeks, within normal noise, and
consistent with the decoupling-based read that the aerobic base is
holding steady rather than moving sharply either way. This week's number
is driven by a genuinely easier week (lower easy HR at a slower pace)
rather than any change in fitness underneath it.

## Race countdown

14 days to Cheltenham (2.0 weeks). Prediction unchanged at **1:22:23**
(range 1:20:09–1:24:37) against your 1:22–1:23 target. Remaining key
sessions: 1 intervals (Wed 9 Sep, the last full interval session), 0 more
tempo, 0 more long runs of consequence — everything else from here is
taper. Taper starts Thursday 10 September, 4 days away.

## Recommendation: **hold**

The plan already does the right thing here on its own: one more full
interval session Wednesday, then taper from the 10th. This week executed
about as close to ideal as any in the block — two tightly judged quality
sessions (2.9 and 0.3 sec/km spreads), a peak-adjacent long run at the
lowest RPE logged all year, achilles silent, and recovery markers flat to
improved despite eight weeks of accumulated load behind it. No changes.

Two things worth a quick answer before Wednesday, neither a plan change:
anything achilles-related since the last two big weeks, and whether
today's low HRV was anything in particular or just noise.

conversation.coach_reply:
Shep — good, that's the answer I was hoping for on both counts. No achilles stiffness or standing-desk ache since the last two big weeks is a genuinely clean signal at exactly the point where a returning prodrome would show up if the load had been too much, and it means the HRV read from Saturday night stays filed as noise rather than a watch item — it didn't show up in execution (Sunday's long run was still RPE 1, flat decoupling) and now it isn't self-reported as anything either. Nothing to revise; the plan holds exactly as written.

So: Wednesday 9 Sep runs as the last full interval session, taper starts Thursday 10th, and this week's read — lowest RPE of the whole build, tightest-judged quality sessions, recovery flat to improved — stands as the strongest week of the block to close on.

On race plan — agreed, next Sunday (13 Sep) is the right moment for it. By then Wednesday's intervals will be done, the taper will be a few days in, and Cheltenham's weather forecast will be close enough to be worth reading properly. That review will cover pacing strategy off the course profile, conditions, the 1:22:23 prediction against your 1:22–83 target, shoes (Fast-R Nitro 3), and the Symbicort/salbutamol race protocol — plus it's the point to actually settle the asthma-nurse preventer conversation, since the cumulative-weeks mechanism means this week is close to the last one where starting it would do anything before the gun. No plan changes needed before then.

conversation.athlete_thoughts: Boddington 10 on 31st Jan.  Club record up for grabs at 1hr and 1min. Feasible?
conversation.coach_reply:
Shep — worth working through properly rather than a gut answer.

Riegel from your current bests puts you close, not clear. The 10K (38:06) and the HM prediction (1:22:23) both put a flat, well-paced 10 miles at roughly 61:50-62:00 today; your sharper 5K (17:48) puts it nearer 61:10. Split that range and the club record of 1:01:00 sits right on your current fitness line — not a stretch, but not banked either. That's actually a reasonably solid answer: 10 miles sits between 10K and HM, so it's a genuinely reliable projection distance, not the long extrapolation a marathon projection is.

Two things move that number in your favour between now and 31 Jan. Cheltenham (20 Sep) replaces Jun/Jul data with a current read, and VO2max is already trending up mid-block (59→60) — so it should land quicker, not slower. And the Manchester base-build between now and January adds aerobic volume, which sharpens 10-mile-type performances even without dedicated speed work.

The real risk isn't fitness, it's freshness. 31 Jan falls in the middle of marathon base-building, which is deliberately a volume phase, not a sharpening one — you can't chase a PB off the back of an unbroken loading week. That's a small ask (a few easy days beforehand), but it means Boddington needs to be built into the Manchester plan as a real fixture with its own short taper, not slotted in around it. I've added it to fixtures.json; we'll plan the taper window around it when we design the marathon block this autumn.

One gap: I don't know the course. Riegel assumes flat and fair — if Boddington has real hills or draws January wind, adjust expectations down. Worth finding out before we plan around it.

No change to the current plan — Wednesday's intervals and the Cheltenham taper stand as agreed.
